name: Web Application
summary: Tools for authorized testing of web applications and their transport security
description: Scanners, fuzzers, proxies and TLS auditors for assessing web applications you own or are contracted to test. Includes content discovery, parameter mining, a SQL-injection tester, HTTP clients and transport-security checks. Several well-known web scanners (Burp Suite, OWASP ZAP, Nikto, Nuclei) are proprietary or not in Debian and are listed separately with official install links.

tools.name: WhatWeb
tools.summary: Identify the technologies a website is built with

tools.name: wafw00f
tools.summary: Identify and fingerprint the web application firewall in front of a site

tools.name: wig

tools.name: DIRB

external.name: Burp Suite
external.summary: Intercepting proxy and web vulnerability scanner
external.license: Proprietary (PortSwigger). A free Community Edition exists with reduced features.

why.text: Burp Suite is closed-source commercial software and cannot be redistributed by SHADOW; PortSwigger provides the installer directly.

how.text: Download the Community or Professional edition installer for Linux from PortSwigger and run it; Professional requires a licence.

external.name: OWASP ZAP
external.summary: Open-source web application scanner and intercepting proxy
external.license: Apache-2.0 (open source), but no current package in Debian.

why.text: ZAP is free and open source but is not currently packaged in Debian; the project ships cross-platform installers and a container image.

how.text: Install from the official Linux installer or run the maintained Docker image as described in the ZAP documentation.

external.name: Nikto
external.summary: Web server scanner for known issues and dangerous files
external.license: GPL-2.0 for the program; Debian files the package under non-free because of the terms of its bundled databases.

why.text: Debian trixie carries Nikto only in the non-free component. Shadow OS uses Debian main only, so no package is offered; upstream recommends running it from a git checkout.

how.text: Clone the official repository and run program/nikto.pl; it needs only Perl, which is already installed.

external.name: Nuclei
external.license: MIT (open source), not packaged in Debian.

why.text: Nuclei and its templates are released on a rapid cadence outside Debian; ProjectDiscovery publishes binaries and an installer.

how.text: Download the release binary for your architecture from the Nuclei releases page, or install with Go; then run nuclei -update-templates.

external.name: feroxbuster
external.summary: Fast recursive content discovery written in Rust
external.license: MIT (open source); not packaged in Debian.

why.text: feroxbuster is distributed as release binaries and a crate, and is not in Debian.

how.text: Download the official release binary, install the published .deb, or build with 'cargo install feroxbuster'.

external.name: DirBuster
external.summary: Classic Java directory and file brute-forcer
external.license: Apache-2.0 (open source); not in Debian (packaged by Kali, not Debian).

why.text: DirBuster is an OWASP Java application packaged downstream (Kali) but not in Debian trixie; ffuf and gobuster, which are in Debian, cover the same need.

how.text: Run the official OWASP ZAP forced-browse add-on, or download DirBuster from the OWASP project.

external.name: Dalfox
external.summary: Powerful XSS scanning and parameter-analysis tool
external.license: MIT (open source); not packaged in Debian.

why.text: Dalfox is a Go tool distributed as release binaries outside Debian.

how.text: Download the release binary for your architecture, or build with 'go install' (Go is in Debian).

external.name: XSStrike
external.summary: Advanced XSS detection and fuzzing suite
external.license: GPL-3.0 (open source); not packaged in Debian.

why.text: XSStrike is a Python tool on GitHub and is not in Debian trixie.

how.text: Clone the official repository and run xsstrike.py with its Python requirements installed.

external.name: Commix
external.license: GPL-3.0 (open source); not currently in Debian trixie.

why.text: Commix is maintained on GitHub and is not in Debian trixie.

how.text: Clone the official repository and run commix.py; it uses only the Python standard library.

external.name: Ghauri
external.license: MIT (open source); not packaged in Debian.

why.text: Ghauri is published on PyPI/GitHub and is not in Debian trixie.

how.text: Install into an isolated environment with pipx ('pipx install ghauri').

external.name: Jaeles
external.license: MIT (open source); not packaged in Debian.

why.text: Jaeles is a Go tool distributed as release binaries outside Debian.

how.text: Download the release binary for your architecture, or build with 'go install' (Go is in Debian).

external.name: Kiterunner
external.summary: Content discovery tuned for API routes and endpoints
external.license: MIT (open source); not packaged in Debian.

why.text: Kiterunner is a Go tool distributed as release binaries outside Debian.

how.text: Download the release archive for Linux and place the kr binary on PATH.

external.name: Skipfish
external.license: Apache-2.0 (open source); not currently in Debian trixie.

why.text: Skipfish is unmaintained upstream and was removed from Debian; build it from the archived source if needed.

how.text: Build from the archived upstream source release; its dependencies (libidn, zlib, pcre) are in Debian.

external.name: Wapiti
external.license: GPL-2.0 (open source); not currently in Debian trixie.

why.text: Wapiti is published on PyPI and is not in Debian trixie.

how.text: Install into an isolated environment with pipx ('pipx install wapiti3').

external.name: Arachni
external.license: Arachni Public Source License (source-available); not packaged in Debian.

why.text: Arachni ships under its own source-available licence and as self-contained bundles, and is not in Debian main.

how.text: Download the official self-contained package for Linux from the Arachni site.

external.name: retire.js
external.summary: Detect JavaScript libraries with known vulnerabilities
external.license: Apache-2.0 (open source); not packaged in Debian.

why.text: retire.js is distributed on npm and is not in Debian trixie.

how.text: Install with npm ('npm install -g retire'); Node.js and npm are in Debian.

external.name: Wappalyzer
external.summary: Identify the technologies a website uses
external.license: Proprietary/open-core; the CLI and data are not packaged in Debian.

why.text: Wappalyzer's current CLI and dataset are distributed via npm and the vendor, not Debian; WhatWeb (in Debian) covers much of the same ground.

how.text: Use the maintained npm package or the browser extension per the Wappalyzer documentation.

external.name: WPScan
external.license: Dual-licensed (WPScan Public Source License); not currently in Debian trixie.

why.text: WPScan ships under its own source-available licence as a Ruby gem and is not in Debian trixie.

how.text: Install the gem with 'gem install wpscan' (Ruby is in Debian); a free API token raises the vulnerability-data limit.
